Our Solution
The safeguarding and privacy focussed platform that puts you in control of your live and on-demand video content

With flexible content capture technology Joymo is a full service end-to-end media streaming platform designed specifically to showcase and grow your sport.

pages.title: Bryanston TV to bring sport, performance and school life… | Joymo
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Bryanston School has partnered with SOCS TV, powered by Joymo, to launch Bryanston TV, a secure, school-branded streaming and video platform for live and on-demand coverage of sport, performing arts, events and wider school life.
Bryanston TV will give pupils, parents, families, Old Bryanstonians and the wider school community a dedicated digital home for key moments across the School, helping them feel closer to life at Bryanston wherever they are in the world.
The platform will enable Bryanston to securely capture, manage and share a wide range of content, from sports fixtures and concerts to performances, talks, ceremonies, pupil showcases and community events, while keeping safeguarding, consent, school control and data protection at the centre.
Bryanston is one of the UK’s leading co-educational boarding and day schools, educating pupils aged 3-18 from its 450 acre campus in Dorset. The school is known for the Bryanston Method, its distinctive approach to education, which encourages pupils to think independently, take ownership of their learning and develop creativity, confidence and individuality.
That same spirit is reflected across Bryanston’s co-curricular life. The school offers around 100 extra-curricular activities each term, spanning sport, arts, music, academic societies, outdoor education and charity programmes. Sport and co-curricular activities are integral to daily life at Bryanston.
Bryanston TV will help bring more of this activity together in one place, allowing the school to celebrate the full breadth of pupil achievement while improving the experience for parents and families.
Hannah Attride, Bryanston’s Chief Commercial Officer, said:
“Bryanston is a community full of energy, creativity and achievement, and we are delighted to be launching Bryanston TV as a way of sharing more of those moments with parents, families and Old Bryanstonians. As we head into our centenary year, we are excited to be able to share these key moments with our community.
From sport and performance to talks, events and pupil-led projects, Bryanston TV will allow our community to feel closer to school life, wherever they are, while ensuring that content is shared in a secure and appropriate way.”
Built for school life: control, safeguarding and quality
SOCS TV, powered by Joymo, is designed specifically for schools. It enables institutions to livestream and publish on-demand content on a dedicated, school-branded platform, while retaining control over access, permissions, content ownership and data.
Key platform benefits include:
- Secure access and safeguarding-first streaming
- School control over content, permissions and retention
- Live and on-demand publishing on a dedicated, branded platform
- Consent-aware workflows and governance tools
- Data protection by design
Marius Larsen, COO/CFO of Joymo, said:
“Bryanston is exactly the kind of school SOCS TV was built for: ambitious, creative, deeply co-curricular and committed to giving pupils opportunities across sport, performance, leadership and wider school life.
With Bryanston TV, the School will have a secure, school-controlled digital home for live and on-demand content — helping parents, families and Old Bryanstonians stay connected to the moments that matter, without compromising safeguarding, consent or data control.
We are proud to support Bryanston with a platform built for education: ownership, governance and quality by design.”
James Kershaw Naylor, Director, Commercial & Product, SOCS, said:
“SOCS TV is a natural extension of how schools already use SOCS to manage and communicate co-curricular life. Schools need tools that fit into the rhythm of busy school environments, support staff rather than add complexity, and give parents a simple, trusted way to stay connected.
Bryanston TV will give the School a school-owned platform for sharing sport, performance and wider school events with its community, while ensuring that access, safeguarding and control remain where they should be: with the School.”
Availability
Bryanston TV is expected to launch for the Autumn Term in 2026. Further details, including how parents and the wider Bryanston community can access the platform, will be announced closer to launch.

pages.title: Joymo and SOCS partner to launch SOCS TV and revolutionise… | Joymo
pages.main_text_excerpt:
SOCS, a trusted leader in school sports and co-curricular management for 25 years, has selected Joymo, the leading direct-to-consumer live video platform for sports rights holders, to develop and build SOCS TV - a pioneering streaming and content management system for the UK and global education sector.
SOCS TV is set to launch this month, providing schools with a secure, high-quality content management system to broadcast events, sports, and activities—while ensuring safeguarding, ease of use, control, and affordability.
With SOCS TV, schools can capture content using anything from state-of-the-art cameras to mobile phones—making it easy to film on the go or during major events. All footage is securely stored on the school’s own platform, not the recording device, ensuring simple, safe, and centralised content management.
The partnership enables SOCS’s school customers - which accounts for over 85% of independent schools in the UK - to take full control of their video content, securely protected behind a registration wall. This ensures privacy, compliance, and new revenue opportunities, while enabling schools to livestream and share events, performances, and co-curricular activities on their own terms.
“Whether showcasing student achievements, broadcasting events, or enhancing learning, SOCS TV makes it simple for schools to share what matters most - safely and securely,“ comments Mike Emery, CEO, Joymo.
“This is a hugely meaningful partnership in terms of digital safeguarding. In the past, higher education partnerships have been seen as media rights or camera technology-led relationships, for Joymo and SOCS safeguarding of content has been paramount in the development of SOCS TV,” Emery added.
“As more schools film fixtures and other key events, much of this content ends up on platforms like YouTube or Vimeo and is stored on personal devices, often without the necessary consent or safeguards in place. We know how important it is to protect children’s privacy. That’s why SOCS TV puts schools fully in control.” says James Kershaw Naylor, Business Development Director, SOCS.
SOCS has built its reputation by seamlessly integrating with leading school management systems, portals, and specialist tools like Return2Play. Now, in response to school feedback, SOCS has partnered with Joymo to create a game-changing video solution for schools.
Founded in 2017, Joymo has a proven track record of delivering tailored media platforms for sports organisations across Europe, the UK, and the USA, covering sports like netball, baseball, basketball, and archery.
SOCS TV is now available for schools looking to enhance their events and sports coverage with a professional-grade streaming solution. Schools can seamlessly integrate SOCS TV within their existing SOCS ecosystem, making live and on-demand streaming effortless.
For more information, visit Joymo for Education.
